HISTORY-HC-007-PRIOR.summary: symptom_history: Surgery occurred 8 days ago for perforated appendicitis. Discharged 4 days ago. Home care included once-daily dressing changes, avoiding lifting more than 10 pounds, keeping the area clean and dry, and monitoring for fever or increased drainage. Patient states spouse has been performing dressing changes and that adherence was good except one missed evening dressing change two days ago.

HISTORY-HC-007-INTERVIEW.summary: symptom_history: Fever began yesterday evening, drainage increased over the last 48 hours, and the wound edge opening was first noticed this morning. Pain is localized to the incision and is worse when standing up from bed. No report of tissue protruding through the wound.

EXAMAUTH-HC-007-GENERAL.authorized_finding: physical_exam_finding: Alert, speaking full sentences, mildly uncomfortable, temperature 38.1 C, heart rate 102 bpm, blood pressure 124/78 mmHg, not hypotensive, and not in septic shock.

EXAMAUTH-HC-007-ABD.authorized_finding: physical_exam_finding: Incision demonstrates localized erythema, seropurulent drainage, mild induration, and approximately 1 cm superficial skin separation. Fascia is not exposed. No evisceration and no diffuse peritoneal signs.

LABAUTH-HC-007-CBC.authorized_result: lab_result_detail: WBC 13.4 x10^9/L with 82 percent neutrophils, hemoglobin 12.6 g/dL, platelets 312 x10^9/L, sodium 137 mmol/L, creatinine 0.8 mg/dL.

CONSULT-HC-007-GENSURG.consult_text: diagnosis_label: Based on postoperative day 8 timing, fever, localized erythema, seropurulent drainage, and only superficial wound-edge separation without visible fascial disruption, the picture favors superficial surgical-site infection over normal healing. Same-day surgical review is indicated to probe the wound, assess depth, and ensure no evolving fascial dehiscence.
